Lakers Nation > Blog > Lakers News > Austin Reaves Tells Funny Rui Hachimura Story Ahead Of First Game Against Former Teammate Lakers News Austin Reaves Tells Funny Rui Hachimura Story Ahead Of First Game Against Former Teammate
 Ron Gutterman Published: 10/23/2026 3 Min Read SACRAMENTO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 26: Rui Hachimura #28 congratulates Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers after they beat the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center on October 26, 2025 in Sacramento, California. Reaves finished with a career high 51 points. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) SHARE The Los Angeles Lakers are 1-0 after a dominant win to start the 2026-27 NBA season. The trio of Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler was even better than advertised. And now, they look to start 2-0 on Friday night as they face Rui Hachimura and the L.A. Clippers. 
 Hachimura left the Lakers and walked over to Inglewood to sign a two-year contract with the Clippers this offseason. He was one of their biggest additions in a summer marred by controversy. And now, he’ll face off against the Lakers for the first time after 3.5 seasons with the team. Reaves, who developed a close bond with Hachimura, joked about his former teammate in preparation of the matchup. 
 “He’s an unbelievable human. I didn’t know if he spoke English for the first two weeks,” Reaves said after practice earlier in the week. “I sat by him on the plane, and he didn’t speak to me, and after that I couldn’t get him to shut up (laughs). So great guy, great player and I miss him.” 
 Hachimura was a beloved figure on the Lakers during his tenure, both for his on-court shooting ability and his off-court personality. It’s clear that his fan favorite status extended to the players on the team, as Reaves has always spoken very highly of his former teammate. 
 The Lakers clearly felt it was in their best interest to move on from Hachimura this offseason, along with nearly the entirety of their core from their playoff run. However, his contributions to the Lakers will always be appreciated. 
 L.A. is in the midst of starting a new era, and part of that process will be trying to land a win against Hachimura’s new team in the Clippers. 
 Austin Reaves believes Lakers can improve after opening night
 Just about everything went the Lakers way in their season opener against the Golden State Warriors. However, this Lakers team is not going to be satisfied with a dominant first game. Reaves said the Lakers still have plenty of room for improvement as they move through the start of the regular season. 
 “It was fun,” Reaves said after the game. “The first quarter, we battled through some things, defensively wasn’t great. But after that, we locked in and played a little faster and was more paying attention to the details. So it was a good first step for us. There’s a lot of things we can get better at, but it was fun.”
